title: Surjectivity on first Tor for a quotient after change of rings
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $J=IA\subseteq A$ the ideal generated by the image of $I$, $M$ an $R$-module, and $N=M\otimes_RA$ its base change to $A$. Choose a free $R$-resolution $F_\bullet\to M$ and a free $A$-resolution $G_\bullet\to N$ with a chain map $F_\bullet\otimes_RA\to G_\bullet$ lifting the identity of $N$. The induced map on first homology $H_1(F_\bullet\otimes_R(A/J))\to H_1(G_\bullet\otimes_A(A/J))$, namely the change-of-rings map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A/J)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(N,A/J)$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MN (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one-trivial, lines 23881--23919); the source uses symmetry of Tor to write the first argument as A/J

proof.text: Base change of the resolution. Let $\cdots\to F_2\xrightarrow{d_2}F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$ be the given free $R$-resolution and put $F'_i=F_i\otimes_RA$, $d'_i=d_i\otimes1_A$, $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon\otimes1_A:F'_0\to N$. Each $F'_i$ is a free $A$-module [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free], $F'_\bullet$ is a complex ($d'_{i-1}d'_i=(d_{i-1}d_i)\otimes1=0$, $\varepsilon'd'_1=0$), and $F'_1\xrightarrow{d'_1}F'_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon'}N\to0$ is exact, by right exactness of $-\otimes_RA$ applied to $F_1\to F_0\to M\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]; in degrees $\ge2$ it need not be exact. Write $P=A/J$. The isomorphisms $c_i:(F_i\otimes_RA)\otimes_AP\cong P\otimes_A(A\otimes_RF_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_RF_i\cong F_i\otimes_RP$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-cancel-base-change] (composed with the symmetry isomorphisms of the tensor product) are natural in $F_i$, hence commute with the differentials and give an isomorphism of complexes $F'_\bullet\otimes_AP\cong F_\bullet\otimes_RP$, so $H_1(F_\bullet\otimes_RP)\cong H_1(F'_\bullet\otimes_AP)$; through it the map of the statement is $H_1(\varphi\otimes_A1_P):H_1(F'_\bullet\otimes_AP)\to H_1(G_\bullet\otimes_AP)$, where $\varphi:F'_\bullet\to G_\bullet$ is the given chain map with $\varepsilon_G\varphi_0=\varepsilon'$. It suffices to show that $H_1(\varphi\otimes1_P)$ is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MN, proof, lines 23888--23891 ('Let $F_2\to F_1\to F_0\to M\to0$ be a free resolution ... Set $F_i'=F_i\otimes_RR'$. The sequence ... may no longer be exact at $F_1'$') and 23897--23899 ('$F_i\otimes_RR'/I'=F_i'/I'F_i'$ ... computes $\mathrm{Tor}_1^R(M,R'/I')$')

proof.text: A free resolution of $N$ containing $F'_\bullet$ (the source's '$F_2'\oplus F_2''\to F_1'\to F_0'\to M'\to0$', continued in all degrees). Define $A$-modules $G'_k$ with differentials $\partial_k:G'_k\to G'_{k-1}$ and $A$-linear inclusions $j_k:F'_k\to G'_k$ by induction on $k$. Put $G'_0=F'_0$, $G'_1=F'_1$, $\partial_1=d'_1$, $j_0,j_1$ the identities, and augmentation $\varepsilon'$. For $k\ge2$, assuming $G'_{k-1},\partial_{k-1},j_{k-1}$ constructed with $\partial_{k-1}j_{k-1}=j_{k-2}d'_{k-1}$, let $Z_{k-1}=\ker\partial_{k-1}\subseteq G'_{k-1}$, let $E_k$ be the free $A$-module with basis $(e_z)_{z\in Z_{k-1}}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and $\iota_k:E_k\to G'_{k-1}$ the $A$-linear map $e_z\mapsto z$, whose image is $Z_{k-1}$. Put $G'_k=F'_k\oplus E_k$, $j_k(x)=(x,0)$ and $\partial_k(x,y)=j_{k-1}(d'_kx)+\iota_k(y)$. Then $\partial_kj_k=j_{k-1}d'_k$, and $\partial_{k-1}\partial_k(x,y)=\partial_{k-1}j_{k-1}d'_kx+\partial_{k-1}\iota_ky=j_{k-2}d'_{k-1}d'_kx+0=0$ (for $k=2$ read $\partial_1\partial_2(x,y)=d'_1d'_2x+d'_1\iota_2y=0$; also $\varepsilon'\partial_1=\varepsilon'd'_1=0$). Exactness [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: at $N$ and at $G'_0$ by Step 1; at $G'_{k-1}$ for $k\ge2$ because $Z_{k-1}=\iota_k(E_k)\subseteq\operatorname{im}\partial_k\subseteq Z_{k-1}$. So $(G'_\bullet,\partial,\varepsilon')$ is a free $A$-resolution of $N$ (each $G'_k$ is a direct sum of two free modules, a basis being the union of the two bases) and $j:F'_\bullet\to G'_\bullet$ is a morphism of complexes, the identity in degrees $0,1$, compatible with the augmentations.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MN, proof, lines 23892--23896 ('A free resolution of $M'$ over $R'$ therefore looks like $F_2'\oplus F_2''\to F_1'\to F_0'\to M'\to0$ for a suitable free module $F_2''$'); the continuation in degrees $\ge3$ is written out here, the source leaves it implicit

proof.text: $H_1(j\otimes1_P)$ is surjective (the source's 'clearly induces a surjection'). In degrees $1$ and $0$ the complexes $F'_\bullet\otimes_AP$ and $G'_\bullet\otimes_AP$ coincide, with the same differential $d'_1\otimes1_P$, and $j_1\otimes1_P$, $j_0\otimes1_P$ are identities. So both have the same module of $1$-cycles $Z=\ker(d'_1\otimes1_P)$, and $H_1(F'_\bullet\otimes P)=Z/\operatorname{im}(d'_2\otimes1_P)$, $H_1(G'_\bullet\otimes P)=Z/\operatorname{im}(\partial_2\otimes1_P)$. Since $\partial_2j_2=d'_2$, $\operatorname{im}(d'_2\otimes1)=\operatorname{im}((\partial_2\otimes1)(j_2\otimes1))\subseteq\operatorname{im}(\partial_2\otimes1)$, and $H_1(j\otimes1_P)$ is the projection $Z/\operatorname{im}(d'_2\otimes1)\to Z/\operatorname{im}(\partial_2\otimes1)$, which is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MN, proof, lines 23899--23919 (the two complexes $F_2'/I'F_2'\oplus F_2''/I'F_2''\to F_1'/I'F_1'\to F_0'/I'F_0'$, the vertical map of complexes, 'clearly induces a surjection on cohomology')

proof.text: Extension of $\varphi$ to $G'_\bullet$. Let $(G_\bullet,\delta,\varepsilon_G)$ be the given free $A$-resolution of $N$ and $\varphi:F'_\bullet\to G_\bullet$ the given chain map, $\varepsilon_G\varphi_0=\varepsilon'$. Define $a_k:G'_k\to G_k$ by induction: $a_0=\varphi_0$, $a_1=\varphi_1$; for $k\ge2$, $a_k(x,y)=\varphi_k(x)+b_k(y)$ where $b_k:E_k\to G_k$ is the $A$-linear map with $b_k(e_z)=g_z$ for a chosen $g_z\in G_k$ with $\delta_kg_z=a_{k-1}(z)$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Such $g_z$ exists: by induction $a$ is a chain map in degrees $\le k-1$ with $a_{k-1}j_{k-1}=\varphi_{k-1}$, so for $z\in Z_{k-1}$ one has $\delta_{k-1}a_{k-1}(z)=a_{k-2}\partial_{k-1}z=0$ (for $k=2$: $\delta_1\varphi_1z=\varphi_0d'_1z=0$), and $G_\bullet$ is exact at $G_{k-1}$ ($k-1\ge1$) [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Then $a_kj_k=\varphi_k$ and $\delta_ka_k(x,y)=\varphi_{k-1}d'_kx+a_{k-1}\iota_ky=a_{k-1}(j_{k-1}d'_kx+\iota_ky)=a_{k-1}\partial_k(x,y)$. So $a:G'_\bullet\to G_\bullet$ is a morphism of complexes with $\varepsilon_Ga_0=\varepsilon'$ (a lift of $\mathrm{id}_N$) and $a\circ j=\varphi$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MN, proof: the source computes $\mathrm{Tor}_1^{R'}$ with the particular resolution of lines 23892--23896; this step compares it with an arbitrary resolution and lift, as the node's statement requires (written by the agent)

proof.text: Conclusion. Free modules are projective [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective], so $G'_\bullet$ and $G_\bullet$ are projective $A$-resolutions of $N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] (1), applied over $A$ with $M=M'=N$, the map $\mathrm{id}_N$ and the lift $a$, one has $H_1(a\otimes1_P)\circ\iota_{G',P}=\iota_{G,P}\circ\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(\mathrm{id}_N,P)=\iota_{G,P}$ (functoriality of Tor [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]), with $\iota_{G',P},\iota_{G,P}$ isomorphisms; hence $H_1(a\otimes1_P)$ is an isomorphism. Since $(a\otimes1_P)\circ(j\otimes1_P)=\varphi\otimes1_P$, $H_1(\varphi\otimes1_P)=H_1(a\otimes1_P)\circ H_1(j\otimes1_P)$ is an isomorphism composed with the surjection of Step 3, hence surjective; by Step 1 so is the map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A/J)=H_1(F_\bullet\otimes_R(A/J))\to H_1(G_\bullet\otimes_A(A/J))=\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(N,A/J)$. (Nothing about $J=IA$ was used: the argument holds for every $A$-module $P$ in place of $A/J$.)
